articles.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL. Our first approach uses static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network for classification, while our second approach uses pre-trained BERT embeddings fine-tuned for the PCL task. articles.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean against Mathlib, optional domain

articles.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem.

articles.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geome

articles.title: Women reach orgasm more often alone, but partnered orgasms are more closely tied to sexual satisfaction
articles.summary: In a survey of nearly 28,000 period-tracking app users, women reported reaching orgasm more often during solo sex than with a partner. Yet it was partnered orgasm frequency, not solo orgasm frequency, that was linked to greater overall sexual satisfaction.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis use linked to higher odds of nighttime breathing problems
articles.summary: A new study links cannabis use to loud snoring and breathing pauses during sleep, with stronger associations among frequent users. The authors suggest that smoke irritation and muscle relaxation in the throat may play a role.

articles.title: Challenges to political beliefs might engage brain networks tied to self-reflection, new study suggests
articles.summary: In a brain imaging study conducted in Poland, people with strong left-wing views barely changed their political beliefs after reading counterarguments, even as they lowered their confidence in factual claims. Their brains also responded differently to the two kinds of challenges.

articles.title: Playing video games with trusted friends may reduce addiction risks
articles.summary: Research reveals that playing video games with a trusted, familiar group of people can build player loyalty while simultaneously reducing the risk of video game addiction. A player's social environment heavily dictates their digital habits.

articles.title: Why do people with psychopathic traits enjoy fear? New psychology research offers a clue
articles.summary: Alfred Hitchcock argued that people enjoy fear only when they feel safe. A study suggests the idea may apply to people with psychopathic traits: a stronger sense of invincibility was linked to feeling less frightened by a horror clip.

articles.title: Scientists identify rare mutations in 36 genes that sharply raise the odds of OCD and tic disorders
articles.summary: A genetic study of nearly 4,000 people with OCD or tic disorders identified 36 genes in which rare damaging mutations sharply raise the odds of these conditions. Most of the genes appear to be shared between the two disorders.
